title: Quantum Computing Fundamentals & Qubits
suggestedQuestions: How does quantum computing differ from classical computing?
What is quantum entanglement and why is it useful?
content: Quantum computing is a rapidly-emerging technology that harnesses the laws of quantum mechanics to solve problems too complex for classical computers. Classical computers encode information in binary bits that can either be 0 or 1. In contrast, quantum computers use quantum bits or qubits. Due to the principle of superposition, a qubit can exist in a multidimensional state representing both 0 and 1 simultaneously until measured. Another key quantum principle is entanglement, where pairs or groups of qubits become interconnected such that the state of one instantly influences the other, regardless of distance. Quantum computers excel at simulation of molecular structures, cryptographic factorization using Shor's algorithm, combinatorial optimization, and material science discovery.

title: Apollo 11 Lunar Landing Mission Overview
suggestedQuestions: Who were the crew members of Apollo 11?
When and where did Apollo 11 land on the Moon?
What was the name of the lunar module?
content: Apollo 11 was the American spaceflight that first landed humans on the Moon on July 20, 1969. Commander Neil Armstrong and Lunar Module Pilot Buzz Aldrin landed the Apollo Lunar Module Eagle at Mare Tranquillitatis (Sea of Tranquility). Armstrong became the first person to step onto the lunar surface six hours and 39 minutes later on July 21, uttering the famous words: 'That's one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.' Command Module Pilot Michael Collins flew the Command and Service Module Columbia alone in lunar orbit while his crewmates were on the surface. Armstrong and Aldrin spent 21 hours and 36 minutes on the lunar surface, collecting 47.5 pounds (21.5 kg) of lunar material before returning to Columbia.

title: Acme Corp Remote Work & Home Office Policy 2026
suggestedQuestions: What is the annual home office stipend amount?
What are the core collaboration hours for remote employees?
How many weeks in advance must international remote work be requested?
content: Acme Corp Remote Work and Equipment Guidelines for 2026: All full-time employees are eligible for hybrid or fully remote arrangements subject to manager approval. Core collaboration hours are 10:00 AM to 3:00 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST), during which team members are expected to be available for synchronous meetings and Slack communication. Acme Corp provides an annual home office equipment stipend of $1,200 per employee, reimbursable for ergonomic chairs, desks, high-speed internet, and monitor displays. For international remote work (working outside the primary country of employment), employees must submit a request at least 4 weeks in advance, and international stints are limited to a maximum of 30 calendar days per calendar year due to tax compliance.

title: Google Gemini 2.5 Flash Architecture & Context Caching
suggestedQuestions: What context window does Gemini 2.5 Flash support?
What is Context Caching and how does it reduce cost?
What is the recommended temperature for factual RAG generation?
content: Gemini 2.5 Flash is Google's high-speed, multimodal model optimized for low-latency reasoning and high-volume tasks. It supports a context window of up to 1 million tokens, allowing extensive document and multimedia analysis. A key feature of the Gemini API is Context Caching, which allows developers to cache frequently queried documents or large system prompts in Gemini's KV cache, reducing input token costs by up to 75% and significantly lowering time-to-first-token latency. For Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) tasks, setting the generation temperature to 0.1 - 0.3 enforces strict factual adherence to the retrieved reference context and eliminates model hallucinations.
